title: SII Vol. 13 No. 26 — Srinivasanallur
location_detail: On the north wall of the Korangunathan temple
summary: This inscription is damaged and a portion of it in the middle is lost

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 27 — Tiruvellarai
location_detail: On the rock in front of the Jambunatha temple
summary: The date of this inscription has been read in the M.E.R. for 1906 as 3 . The letters look more and this seems to be the correct reading, since we have not come across a date later than the 27th year for any king bearing the mere name Rajakesarivarman

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 28
location_detail: On the same rock
summary: This records another endowment of money made by a member of the Manigramam of Uraiyur for a similar purpose

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 29 — Tirumalpuram
location_detail: On the west wall of the central shrine, Manikanthesvara temple
summary: This records an endowment of 15 kalanju of gold by Madhurantakan Gandaradittan for the daily supply of an ulakku of oil for a lamp in the temple of Tirumalperralvar, to be made by the urar (assembly) of Serugur in Valla-nadu, a division of Damar-kottam, in whose charge the amount was left by the don

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 30
location_detail: On the north, west and south walls of the same shrine
summary: This registers a sale of land by Kambattadigal, son of Kandichchi Mapparradigal of Tirumarperu in Valla-nadu of Damr-kottam, to Madhrantakan Gandaradittan who endowed it for a lamp in the temple

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 32
location_detail: On the same wall
summary: This is identical with No. 285 of 1906 (No. 29 above)

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 33
location_detail: On the south wall of the central shrine, ruined Vishnu temple in the same village
summary: It consists of two portions, a Sanskrit verse and a Tamil prose passage recording the same grant, viz., a gift of 30 Suvarnas (gold coins-kalanju ?) by Aditya for feeding a Brahmana in a matha at Govindapadi

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 34
location_detail: On the same wall
date_text: This is engraved almost as a continuation of, and in the same script as No. 311 of 1906 of the 34th year of Parantaka I
summary: This inscription records both in Sanskrit and in Tamil the provision made for burning a lamp in the temple of Perumanadigal Kamasari, i.e., Krishna, in the Sanskrit portion) at Govindapadi by a Vellala resident of Kulakkudi in Pidavur-nadu, a subdivision of Irungolapadi

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 37 — Tiruvidaimarudur
location_detail: On the north wall of the central shrine, Mahalingasvamin temple
summary: This is an incomplete inscription recording probably some gift of land

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 38
location_detail: On the south wall of the same shrine
summary: The inscription records an endowment of 6 Karunkasu (the same as Ilakkasu ?) entrusted with the Senaiyar (Military body) of the place, for the daily supply of two tender cocoanuts for offering after the midday worship, to god Mahadeva of the Mulasthana at Tiruvidaimarudil in Tiraimur-nadu on the sou

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 39 — Tiruvisalur
location_detail: On the north wall of thecentral shrine, Sivayoganathasvamin temple
summary: It registers a gift of land made tax-free after purchase, by Siddhavadavan Suttiyar, a queen of Uttama-Chola and daughter of a Miladu chief (name not given), to provide for 108 pots of water for the sacred bath on the day of sankranti every month, of the god (Paramasvami) at Tiruvisalur in Amaninara

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 39 — Avaninarayana-chaturvedimangalam
location_detail: above for the sacred bath of god Tiruvisalur-Paramasvami at Avaninarayana-chaturvedimangalam
summary: This is also evidently a record of Rajaraja I

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 42 — Tirunedungulam
location_detail: On the south wall of the Ganesa shrine, Nedungalanathasvamin temple
summary: The inscription registers an endowment of land after reclamation, which was left in charge of the sthanikas of the temple, by a certain . . . . . . . . . . midayan Varadan alias Arumunikanda-Perunayar for offerings of rice twice a day to the image of Likasundara set up in the temple of the god at Ti

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 43 — Tiruvadandai
location_detail: On the south wall of the central shrine, Varaha-Perumal temple
summary: This records an agreement given by the sabha of Madambakkam (s. a

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 44 — Kumbhakonam
location_detail: On the north wall of thecentral shrine, Nagesvara temple
summary: This records a sale of a quarter portion (or veli ?) of land (karchey) by the Mulaparishad of Tirukkudamukkil, a devadana in Pambur-nadu on the northern bank (of the Kaveri), to a certain Aravan Kalangamalai, a Vellala resident of Tanjavur who endowed it to the temple of Tirukkilkottattu-Paramasvami

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 45
location_detail: On the same wall
summary: This records a gift of 90 sheep for a perpetual lamp in the temple of Paramasvami of Kilkottam, by Kumaran Tudu[va]n, a Kaikkola resident of Tanjavur who was a member of the Virasola-terinja-Kaikkolar (community or regiment)

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 46
location_detail: On the south wall of the same shrine
summary: It seems to register a sale of 10 veli of land, including a portion situated at Arisalur which had been granted to the Mulaparadaip-Perumakkal of Tirukkudamukkil (by the king) as abhisheka-dakshinai to the temple of Tirukkikottattu-[Parama]svami in return for 1500 kalanju

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 47 — Tillasthanam
location_detail: On the south wall of the central shrine, Ghritasthanesvara temple
summary: This is an unfinished inscription in which two persons are mentioned evidently as donors to the temple of Mahadeva at Tiruneyttanam, a devadana of Kilpilaru in Poygai-nadu

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 48
location_detail: On the same wall
summary: This is another unfinished inscription mentioning a gift to the same temple on behalf of Mallan Araiyan of the Samarakesarit-trinja-Kaikkolar (community or regiment)

title: SII Vol. 13 No. 49 — Erumbur
location_detail: On the north wall of the central shrine, Kadambavanesvara temple
summary: This records an endowment of 7 ma of land to provide for the daily offering of rice to thedeity in the temple of Siru-Tirukkoyil-Perumanadigal at Urumur in Nalvayalur-kurram by Aritan Kannan Kannan of the village
